turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I've the INR up on the screen, it's 3.8.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks a million. Come on in, sit in by the desk. How are you keeping?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Uh, what has you in today?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Warfarin.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Sorry, the wheel's caught on the— there now. I do the mornings with her.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're very welcome. So, the warfarin. Any bleeding, any bruising, any blood when you go to the toilet?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): And nosebleeds?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0011] person_1 (NURSE): I grabbed the vitals outside. Pulse 92, a bit jumpy. Blood pressure 146 over 84.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely, thanks. Are you still on 5 milligrams of warfarin every evening for the fibrillation?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0014] person_4 (CAREGIVER): There's the antibiotic as well, out of hours, your man started her on—
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): On what, sorry, I cut across you.
[SEG0016] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Uh, clarithromicin, 500 twice a day, for the chest. Since Saturday.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right so. Is the cough still there?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Cough.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Umm, bringing up any phlegm, or a fever with it?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has that cough been at you?
[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She was at the bingo on Tuesday and then the—
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): A week.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): A week, ok. Any pain in the chest, or getting short of breath?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Now the greens. Cabbage, kale, spinach, any change in that lately? It moves the INR around.
[SEG0027] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She's after dropping them altogether. Hardly a leaf of cabbage or kale. She just went off the notion.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): That'll push it up. Less vitamin K, and the clarithromycin does the same. I'm not a bit surprised the INR is 3.8, a bit high for the fibrillation.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness, or blackouts?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit about the family. Heart, sugar, pressure, whoever comes to mind.

[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties. Mother did not. Another sister has pressure but no sugar. The husband is on the metformin, that's his not mine, and my sister takes biotin for the hair, I don't take either.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted, none of those are your tablets. You still have the atrial fibrillation yourself?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0037] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And bisoprolol, 2.5 in the morning, for the heart rate. I put it out with the tea.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets of your own?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): What's the shape of the week for you, work, food, getting out, a drink, all that?

[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): I do the books for the son's garage still. Four mornings, about twenty hours. Dinner is potatoes and a bit of meat, not much veg these days, and I walk the dog to the end of the road. A glass of wine of a Sunday, and I don't smoke.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair play. I'll just have a listen, if you don't mind.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Heart's irregularly irregular, no murmur. Lungs are clear, which is reassuring with that cough.
[SEG0046] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Will she manage the bus after, we've the—
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): She will, sure, nothing heavy today. I'm going to ease the warfarin. I nearly said 3.5, err, actually we'll make it 4 milligrams every evening instead of the 5.
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): Four.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Four, yes. Finish the clarithromycin, don't leave it off early. Keep the greens the same small amount each day, no sudden big plate of cabbage.
[SEG0050] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll mind the cabbage so.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. I'll book the INR for a week from today, and I want you back in here the same day. A week, not an if.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0053] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put that INR in the book for next week.

social_history.description: Does the books for her son's garage
Works 4 mornings a week, about 20 hours
Potatoes and a bit of meat, not much veg these days
Dropped cabbage and kale altogether; hardly a leaf
Walks the dog to the end of the road
A glass of wine on a Sunday
Does not smoke

clinical_assessment.assessment: INR is high at 3.8, likely from less vitamin K and clarithromycin
clinical_assessment.normalized_assessment: Supratherapeutic INR secondary to reduced vitamin K intake and clarithromycin
clinical_assessment.basis: INR 3.8, reduced cabbage and kale, clarithromycin

clinical_actions.description: Book INR
Reduce warfarin to 4 mg every evening
Finish the clarithromycin course and do not stop it early
Keep green vegetables at the same small amount each day and avoid a sudden large portion of cabbage
Follow-up consultation

spec.situation: Older patient on warfarin for atrial fibrillation; INR result read aloud; antibiotic started elsewhere; green leafy diet changes; dose adjusted and recheck in a week.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Diet supported, but 'cabbage and kale dropped' was reported by caregiver, not patient.
bad.text: diet (description=Potatoes and a bit of meat, not much veg these days; cabbage and kale dropped, status=current, reported_by=patient)
